newsitem.title: USA: NHL ice hockey-PENGUINS NAME KEVIN CONSTANTINE NEW COACH.
newsitem.headline: NHL ice hockey-PENGUINS NAME KEVIN CONSTANTINE NEW COACH.

text.p: The post-Mario Lemieux era in Pittsburgh will will begin with a new coach behind the Penguins bench after the team named Calgary Flames assistant Kevin Constantine to the post on Thursday.

The 38-year-old Constantine takes over for general manager Craig Patrick, who came down from the front office and appointed himself interim coach after relieving Eddie Johnston of his duties in March.
In his previous stint as a NHL head coach, Constantine compiled a 55-78-24 record in two-plus seasons with the expansion San Jose Sharks (1993-95).
He led the Sharks to a league-record 58-point improvement in his first season with the club and a first-round playoff upset of the top-seeded Detroit Red Wings that year (1994).

Constantine takes over a team that will begin life without its superstar captain and six-time league scoring leader Lemieux, who decided to hang up his Hall of Fame-bound skates at the end of the 1996-97 campaign.
Patrick, a former Penguins' head coach, replaced Johnston on March 3 when the team was 31-26-5.
Pittsburgh finished second in the Northeast Division at 38-36-8 and lost in five games in the opening round of the Stanley Cup playoffs to the Philadelphia Flyers.
